page: Vultr vx1-m-2c-16g-120s is a shared-CPU instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 2 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, mapped to 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Storage is bundled as a 120 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512_VNNI and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark data shows a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-threaded performance is strong, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 25% of tested servers. However, because the 2 vCPUs share a single physical core, multi-core performance is constrained, with the stress-ng multi-core metric and PassMark CPU score falling into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is mixed; while large-block read and write bandwidths are average, small-block cached read bandwidth is weak. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the bottom 25%, reflecting the shared CPU limitations.

This server offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained, independent multi-core processing. The high resource density of 16.0 GB RAM on a shared 2-vCPU footprint allows for larger in-memory datasets without the cost of dedicated compute cores. However, the shared CPU allocation introduces performance variability under heavy parallel loads, as evidenced by poor text generation speeds on medium-sized language models. This configuration is suitable for lightweight caching layers, memory-bound utility scripts, single-threaded data processing, and static web serving, where static throughput benchmarks average 6.84 GB/sec.
